findings.text: the third negative control says "nesting requiredness inside `params` fails the last case", but the case it can actually falsify is the fifth (:321), which asserts the pre-§13 parent still reads `params` as a list of names; nesting requiredness inside `params` breaks that reading, while the last case (:322) measures only that the child's verdict is authoritative and is unaffected by the shape of `params`

findings.reason: without a sentence making the verdict itself the routing trigger, an implementer who only drops the refusal satisfies no-reconnect but leaves case 1's `schema_note` unreachable on the documented path, and the fix that suggests itself is weakening case 1 rather than routing the call.
findings.text: "A compatible change is served on current code with no refusal, and its answer carries a `schema_note`" presupposes that a call of a compatibly-changed tool is routed to the child, but the plan's own routing rule (:270, §11) sends a call to the child only when the tool has already fallen back, and returns a successful image answer untouched, so on the stated mechanism a compatible change that the image can still answer is never served from current code and can carry no `schema_note`
